claim: The COVID-19 outbreak caused more than 30,000 deaths in Lombardy alone up to the end of March 2021.
source: Starting from late February 2020, the COVID-19 outbreak struck the north of Italy causing more than 30,000 deaths in Lombardy alone, up to the end of March 2021.
evidence: This is a factual statement about mortality statistics in Lombardy during the COVID-19 outbreak.

claim: At the beginning of the outbreak, the number of severely ill patients seeking admission to the emergency department exceeded available resources at Spedali Civili di Brescia.
source: At the beginning of the outbreak, the Spedali Civili di Brescia (SCBH), the university hospital of one of the hardest hit cities in Europe, was faced with a 'flash flood' of severely ill patients seeking admission to the emergency department (ED). For several weeks, their number exceeded the available resources, obliging a continuous organizational restructuring of the hospital wards (Garrafa et al., 2020b).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Garrafa et al., 2020b describing the hospital's experience.

claim: A chest X-ray severity score (Brescia X-ray score) was developed to grade pulmonary involvement and track changes objectively over time.
source: With the purpose of grading pulmonary involvement and tracking changes objectively over time, a chest X-ray severity score was developed (Brescia X-ray score) (Borghesi and Maroldi, 2020; Maroldi et al., 2021; Borghesi et al., 2020a; Borghesi et al., 2020b).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations describing the development of the Brescia X-ray score.

claim: The Brescia X-ray score was able to predict in-hospital mortality in 302 patients.
source: The score was able to predict in-hospital mortality in 302 patients.
evidence: This is a statement about the predictive capability of the score based on a specific patient cohort.

claim: The study enrolled 2782 patients between March 2020 and December 2020.
